summary.short: Supplements the UK GDPR and regulates personal data processing by controllers, law enforcement competent authorities and intelligence services, with data subject rights, automated decision-making limits, transfer rules and the Information Commission. Enacted 23 May 2018.
summary.long: The Act supplements the UK GDPR, which governs most personal data processing (ss.1-4), and regulates processing by law enforcement competent authorities (Part 3) and intelligence services (Part 4). Part 2 covers general processing, special category data (s.10), exemptions (ss.15-16), certification providers (s.17) and significant decisions based solely on automated processing (ss.50A-50D). Part 3 sets six principles (ss.35-40), data subject rights (ss.44-54), controller and processor duties (ss.56-71) and third-country transfer conditions (ss.73-78). Part 4 applies parallel principles and rights (ss.86-100), designation notices for qualifying competent authorities (ss.82A-82E) and transfer limits (s.109). Part 5 establishes the Information Commission (s.114A), which may issue standard data protection clauses (s.119A) and enforcement and penalty notices, including administrative fines (s.115(8)-(9)). Parts 6 and 7 are listed in s.1 but their text is not in the extract, which ends at s.120. The Act is dated 23 May 2018.
